response.reason: The Kahan correction term itself is uncompensated float32: when the +2^30 interior term lands in `correction`, any small low-values already accumulated there (or added before the -2^30 term arrives) are rounded away, since ulp(2^30)=128 » the ~1-magnitude lows, so those lows vanish from the final row sum. Exactness requires the permuted interior to place both ±2^30 entries before all eight lows (~1/45 chance); the probe outputs (row-mean ≈6.75 vs expected ≈8.0 for eight uniform(0.25,1.75) lows per row) are statistically consistent with at least one low being dropped, giving relative error far above 1e-5.
